title: Introduction to Networks
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This TCP port number carries unencrypted web traffic

categoryLegend: Ports & Protocols: 80, 443, 22, 53, 25.  Network Hardware: hub, switch, router, AP, firewall.  Models & Transport: OSI layers, TCP, UDP, handshake, ARP.  IP Addressing & SOHO: subnet mask, gateway, RFC 1918, NAT.  Wireless & Cabling: 802.11, channels, WPA, Cat 6, T568.  Tools & Services: ping, tracert, DNS, DHCP, VLAN.

clues.clue: This TCP port number carries unencrypted web traffic.
clues.explain: HTTP uses TCP port 80 for standard, unencrypted web browsing. Any data sent over port 80 is transmitted in plaintext and can be intercepted.

clues.clue: This TCP port is used by SSH to provide encrypted remote terminal access, and it is also the default port for SFTP.
clues.explain: SSH (Secure Shell) operates on TCP port 22 and provides an encrypted channel for remote login and command execution. SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) rides over the same SSH session on port 22.

clues.clue: DHCP clients send their Discover and Request broadcasts to this UDP port on the server, while the server replies from port 67.
clues.explain: DHCP uses UDP port 67 for the server side and UDP port 68 for the client side. Clients broadcast from port 68 to port 67 during the DORA process to obtain an IP address.

clues.clue: This range of port numbers — 49152 through 65535 — is assigned automatically by the OS for short-lived outbound connections and is sometimes called the ephemeral range.
clues.explain: The IANA defines port numbers 49152–65535 as dynamic or private ports, used by the operating system as temporary source ports for client-side connections. They are not assigned to specific services.

clues.clue: Secure IMAP email retrieval uses this TCP port, while its unencrypted counterpart runs on port 143.
clues.explain: IMAPS (IMAP over TLS/SSL) uses TCP port 993 to encrypt email retrieval between a client and a mail server. Unencrypted IMAP uses TCP port 143.

clues.clue: This Layer 2 device learns MAC addresses and forwards frames only to the correct port, reducing unnecessary traffic on the network.
clues.explain: A switch operates at OSI Layer 2 (Data Link) and builds a MAC address table by inspecting incoming frames. It forwards each frame only to the port where the destination MAC address is known, unlike a hub which broadcasts to all ports.

clues.clue: This device operates at OSI Layer 3, connects separate networks, and makes forwarding decisions based on IP addresses.
clues.explain: A router works at OSI Layer 3 (Network) and uses routing tables to forward packets between different networks based on destination IP addresses. It also commonly performs NAT to allow private addresses to reach the internet.

clues.clue: This outdated Layer 1 device forwards every incoming signal out of all its other ports, creating a single collision domain for all connected devices.
clues.explain: A hub is a passive Layer 1 device with no intelligence — it simply repeats electrical signals to every port. All devices share one collision domain, which severely degrades performance as the number of connected devices grows.

clues.clue: This IEEE standard allows a single Ethernet cable to carry both data and electrical power simultaneously, commonly used to power wireless access points and IP cameras.
clues.response: What is PoE (Power over Ethernet) — IEEE 802.3af/at/bt?
clues.explain: Power over Ethernet (PoE) is defined by IEEE 802.3af (15.4W), 802.3at (30W), and 802.3bt (up to 90W). It eliminates the need for a separate power supply by delivering DC power through standard Cat5e or better Ethernet cabling.

clues.clue: Unlike an unmanaged switch, this type of switch supports features such as VLANs, SNMP monitoring, and PoE configuration through an administrative interface.
clues.explain: A managed switch provides an administrative interface (CLI, web GUI, or SNMP) that allows network administrators to configure VLANs, quality of service, port security, and PoE budgets. Unmanaged switches operate with no configuration options.

clues.clue: In the OSI model, this layer number is where IP addressing and routing decisions take place.
clues.explain: OSI Layer 3, the Network layer, is responsible for logical addressing using IP and for routing packets across multiple networks. Routers and ICMP both operate at this layer.

clues.clue: TCP establishes a connection using this three-message sequence before any data is transferred.
clues.response: What is the three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)?
clues.explain: TCP begins every connection with a three-way handshake: the client sends SYN, the server replies with SYN-ACK, and the client responds with ACK. This exchange synchronizes sequence numbers and confirms both sides are ready to communicate.

clues.clue: This connectionless Layer 4 protocol sacrifices reliability and ordering guarantees in exchange for low latency, making it ideal for DNS queries and real-time streaming.
clues.explain: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol that sends datagrams with no acknowledgment, retransmission, or ordering mechanism. Applications that can tolerate some packet loss — such as DNS, DHCP, and media streaming — choose UDP for its lower overhead.

clues.clue: This Layer 3 protocol is used by the ping command and by routers to send error and diagnostic messages, such as 'destination unreachable.'
clues.response: What is ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol)?
clues.explain: ICMP operates at OSI Layer 3 and is used for network diagnostics and error reporting. The ping utility sends ICMP Echo Request messages and listens for Echo Reply messages to test reachability and measure round-trip time.

clues.clue: This Layer 3 protocol resolves a known IP address to its corresponding MAC address so that a frame can be delivered on the local network segment.
clues.explain: ARP maps an IPv4 address to a MAC address within the same broadcast domain. A host broadcasts an ARP Request asking 'Who has this IP?' and the device with that IP replies with its MAC address so the sender can build the correct Ethernet frame.

clues.clue: An IPv4 address consists of this many bits, written as four decimal octets separated by dots.
clues.explain: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses divided into four 8-bit octets, each expressed as a decimal number from 0 to 255. An example address is 192.168.1.100.

clues.clue: This private IPv4 address range, starting at 192.168.0.0 with a /16 prefix, is the most commonly found in home and small-office routers.
clues.explain: RFC 1918 defines 192.168.0.0/16 as a private address block not routable on the public internet. Home routers commonly assign addresses in the 192.168.1.x or 192.168.0.x range from this block.

clues.clue: During the DHCP lease process, this is the first message a client broadcasts onto the network when it needs an IP address.
clues.explain: The DORA process begins with a DHCP Discover, a broadcast sent by a client with no IP address to locate available DHCP servers on the local network. The server then responds with a DHCP Offer containing a proposed IP address and lease parameters.

clues.clue: A subnet mask of 255.255.255.0, written in CIDR notation as /24, means this many bits identify the host portion of the address.
clues.explain: A /24 prefix allocates 24 bits to the network portion, leaving 8 bits for the host portion. This allows for 256 addresses (0–255) in the range, with 254 usable host addresses after reserving the network and broadcast addresses.

clues.clue: PAT (Port Address Translation) allows many devices sharing one public IP address to maintain unique sessions by differentiating each connection using this field in the transport header.
clues.response: What is the source port number?
clues.explain: PAT is a form of NAT that maps multiple private IP:port pairs to a single public IP address using unique source port numbers for each outbound session. The router tracks these mappings in a NAT translation table to correctly return responses to each private host.

clues.clue: This is the human-readable name a Wi-Fi network broadcasts so that nearby devices can find it and connect.
clues.response: What is the SSID (Service Set Identifier)?
clues.explain: The SSID (Service Set Identifier) is the wireless network's name; an access point broadcasts it so client devices can discover and join the network.

clues.clue: The maximum segment length for standard Ethernet over copper twisted-pair cabling is this many meters.
clues.explain: The IEEE 802.3 Ethernet standard specifies a maximum copper cable run of 100 meters (approximately 328 feet) for 10BASE-T, 100BASE-TX, and 1000BASE-T. Beyond this distance, signal attenuation causes errors and requires a repeater or switch.

clues.clue: This deprecated wireless security protocol used the RC4 stream cipher and is considered broken; it was the first WPA standard's predecessor.
clues.explain: WEP was the original 802.11 security protocol and relied on the RC4 cipher with a weak IV implementation that made it trivially crackable within minutes. It has been deprecated and replaced by WPA2 (AES-CCMP) as the current minimum standard.

clues.clue: On the 2.4 GHz band, these three channel numbers are non-overlapping and should be used on adjacent access points to avoid co-channel interference.
clues.explain: The 2.4 GHz band has 11 channels in North America, but adjacent channels overlap. Channels 1, 6, and 11 are spaced 25 MHz apart — enough separation to avoid overlapping — and are the only three fully non-overlapping channels in the band.

clues.clue: Cat6a cabling supports 10 Gbps Ethernet at full 100-meter runs, while standard Cat6 is limited to 10 Gbps only up to this shorter distance.
clues.explain: Cat6 supports 10GBASE-T (10 Gbps) only up to 55 meters due to increased crosstalk at higher frequencies. Cat6a adds additional shielding and tighter twists to maintain 10 Gbps performance over the full 100-meter standard Ethernet distance.

clues.clue: This command-line utility sends ICMP Echo Request packets to a target host to test whether it is reachable and to measure round-trip time.
clues.explain: Ping is a basic network diagnostic tool available on all major operating systems. It transmits ICMP Echo Request messages and displays the Echo Reply times (in milliseconds), confirming connectivity and providing a basic latency measurement.

clues.clue: On a Windows system, this command displays the local machine's IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and MAC address when run with the /all flag.
clues.explain: The ipconfig command is the Windows tool for viewing IP configuration details. Running ipconfig /all reveals the full configuration including the physical (MAC) address, DHCP lease information, DNS server addresses, and gateway.

clues.clue: This command-line tool traces the path packets take to a destination by sending probes with incrementing TTL values and recording each router hop along the route.
clues.explain: Tracert (Windows) and traceroute (Linux/macOS) discover the path to a destination by sending packets with TTL values starting at 1. Each router that drops a packet because TTL reached zero sends back an ICMP Time Exceeded message, revealing that hop's IP address.

clues.clue: DNS resolution follows a hierarchy where a client's configured resolver first checks its cache, then queries a root server, then a TLD server, and finally this type of server that holds the actual records for a domain.
clues.response: What is an authoritative name server?
clues.explain: An authoritative DNS server holds the actual DNS zone records (A, MX, CNAME, etc.) for a specific domain and provides a definitive answer. The recursive resolver contacts root servers to find the TLD, then the TLD to find the authoritative server, which returns the final answer.

clues.clue: NTP organizes time sources into numbered levels called this, where level 0 is an atomic clock and each subsequent level represents one hop further from that reference.
clues.explain: NTP uses a stratum hierarchy to describe distance from a reference clock. A Stratum 0 device is a high-precision clock (GPS, atomic); a Stratum 1 server is directly connected to it; a Stratum 2 server syncs from Stratum 1, and so on. Higher stratum numbers mean more hops and potentially less accuracy.
